summary: An indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Georg von Simson studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1958–1965). He served at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) and as professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Specializing in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology, he studied at the University of Jena, TU Dresden, and the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), joining the Prussian Academy of Sciences in 1889.

George A. Kennedy was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke (~1934–1937). He subsequently held a post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Keyworth studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD at UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held a professorship at the University of Colorado Boulder (2001) and served as associate professor at the University of Saskatchewan.

A linguist and indologist, Grierson studied at Shrewsbury School and Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1907), headed the Linguistic Survey of India as Superintendent (1898–1928), and was a Governor at SOAS (1917–1925).
An Indologist, George Adolphus Jacob served as a colonel in the Bombay Staff Corps (attested 1888) and the Indian Army (attested 1909), and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (attested 1894).

George Baumann, an Indologist, completed his PhD at Heidelberg University (~1969–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (~1973–1975). He worked at the University of Tübingen (~1975–2001) and Tübingen University Library (1976–2001).
George C. O. Haas was an Indologist who served as Recording Secretary of the American Oriental Society (~1913–1918) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1916–1918).

An Indologist and linguist, Cardona studied at NYU, earned his PhD at Yale under Paul Thieme (~1958–1960), and studied under traditional Indian teachers. He spent his career as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–2005).

An Indologist and philosopher, George Chemparathy studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1962–1968) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as professor at Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

A history and archaeology scholar, George Cowgill studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1987) and Arizona State University (~1987–2018).

A philosopher, George Croom Robertson studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1862–1863). He served on the faculty at University College London from circa 1866 until 1892.

A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology, Cœdès studied at the EPHE and Humboldt University of Berlin. He directed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1929–1947), later teaching at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and other Parisian institutions.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Bond studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972). He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University from circa 1974 to 2012.

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

A linguist and indologist, Dunkel completed his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978) and Princeton University (1978–1986) before taking the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Zurich in 1986.

A scholar of religious studies, Moore studied at Yale University (1870–1872) and Union Theological Seminary (~1874–1877). He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Harvard University (1902; Frothingham Professor 1904–1928), and a guest professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1910).
A philosopher, George Herbert Palmer studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He held an academic post at Harvard University from circa 1870 to 1913.

An indologist and linguist, Hart earned a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard (~1964–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1974 until becoming professor emeritus around 2014.

A linguist and philosopher, Lakoff studied at MIT (~1959–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1963–1966). He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley (1972–2016).
